story.head: The Red Wings played last night
paras: The Lightning (8-3-1) beat Winnipeg 6-4 on Thursday, and the Red Wings have won two in a row. The Red Wings played last night, and the Bolts are rested. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Red Wings last (tied for 16th in the NHL) and the Lightning fourth (tied for tenth). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Red Wings have played better than their record (.577) says: their chances are worth about .634, and their finishing has held them back. The Lightning’s record (.708) is about what their chances are worth.

The Red Wings draw more penalties than they take (2nd) and have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (3rd). They also block more shots than almost anyone (2nd), so the Red Wings are likely to get in the way of a lot of the Lightning’s shots. The Lightning get into more chippy games than anyone (1st), rarely ice the puck (2nd) and keep shots away from their net (3rd). The Red Wings’ power play against the Lightning’s penalty killers is strength against strength.

Alex DeBrincat (6 G / 9 A / 15 P in 13 GP) leads the Red Wings in scoring. Viktor Arvidsson (8 G / 6 A / 14 P in 13 GP) has a team-high eight goals, with nine points in his last five games. For the Lightning, Brandon Hagel (8 G / 8 A / 16 P in 12 GP) leads the way in scoring. Nikita Kucherov (4 G / 11 A / 15 P in 12 GP) isn’t far behind, with seven points in his last five games.
Daniil Tarasov (1-0-2 / .940 SV% in 3 GS) will likely start for Detroit, and Andrei Vasilevskiy (6-3-0 / .876 SV% in 9 GS) for Tampa Bay.
At home, Jon Cooper likes to send Hagel, Cirelli and Holmberg out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against DeBrincat, Finnie and Arvidsson.
